title: skill-prefs: the Description guidance

source.note: A newer draft of the guidance on writing a skill's description. The committed file holds an older, shorter Trigger bullet in its place.

gist: Defines a skill's description by the one decision it serves and the budget it lives under, draws the rules for writing it from those two facts, and closes with the exception for skills that are only summoned.

context.why: The document the passage belongs to, as committed. Its Trigger bullet is the older version of sentence 5.
The skill sentence 5 cites as its cautionary case.

description.label: description
description.gloss: The description value in a SKILL.md file's YAML frontmatter.

ctx.quote: description: "Standing preferences for how a skill should be written.

listing.label: listing
listing.gloss: The list of available skills, by name and description, that a session sees before loading any of them.

session.label: session
session.gloss: One running conversation with the model.

load-decision.label: the decision about what to load
load-decision.gloss: The session's choice of which skills to load for the request in front of it.

budget.label: budget
budget.gloss: A limit on how much text the listing can hold. The passage gives neither its size nor its unit.

situation.label: the summoning situation
situation.gloss: The kind of request or circumstance in which the skill should be used.

material.label: material
material.gloss: What the skill produces when it runs. For inspire-excellence, the prompts it writes.

inspire-excellence.label: inspire-excellence
inspire-excellence.gloss: A skill in the web-tools skill library that helps write high-ambition prompts. Its description says it triggers on any ask to write a prompt with conviction behind it.

ctx.quote: Helps construct a high-ambition prompt that hands over a standard and a direction rather than a feature spec.
Triggers include any ask to write a prompt with conviction behind it.

trigger.label: trigger
trigger.gloss: The part of a description that says when to use the skill, which sentence 4 calls the situation that summons it. The committed version of this guidance is headed Trigger and states sentence 5's rule in nearly the same words.

ctx.quote: The trigger should name the situation that summons the skill, never the material it produces.

boundary.label: boundary
boundary.gloss: A clause in a description saying what the skill is not for and which skill to use instead.

body.label: body
body.gloss: The SKILL.md text below the frontmatter, which a session reads only after loading the skill.

summoned-only.label: summoned-only skill
summoned-only.gloss: A skill that runs only when a user calls it by name, never loaded on the model's own judgment.

disable-model-invocation.label: disable-model-invocation
disable-model-invocation.gloss: A frontmatter flag that declares a skill summoned-only.

ctx.quote: In Claude Code a skill can declare its mode in frontmatter

sentences.text: The description is the skill's entry in a listing a session scans to decide what to load.

atoms.claim: A skill's description is its entry in the skill listing.
atoms.quote: the skill's entry in a listing

atoms.claim: A session scans the skill listing to decide which skills to load.
atoms.quote: a session scans to decide what to load

sentences.text: The listing has a budget: past it, descriptions drop and names remain, least-used skills first.

atoms.claim: The skill listing has a size budget.
atoms.quote: The listing has a budget

atoms.claim: Once the listing exceeds its budget, skills lose their descriptions from it and keep only their names.
atoms.quote: descriptions drop and names remain

atoms.claim: The least-used skills lose their descriptions first.
atoms.quote: least-used skills first

atoms.claim: Write a skill's description to serve a session's decision about which skills to load.
atoms.quote: Write for that one decision

atoms.claim: A skill's description should serve no purpose other than the decision about what to load.
atoms.quote: one decision
atoms.note: The word 'one' makes the purpose exclusive. Sentence 7 relies on that exclusivity.

sentences.text: Lead with what the skill does, a verb and its object, then the situation that summons it, in the words a request would use: one or two phrases, not a list of synonyms.

links.here: Lead with what the skill does
links.gloss: Says what writing for the decision about what to load means in practice: what goes first in the description, and what follows.

atoms.claim: Open a skill's description with what the skill does, as a verb and its object.
atoms.quote: Lead with what the skill does, a verb and its object

atoms.claim: After what the skill does, the description states the situation in which the skill should be used.
atoms.quote: then the situation that summons it

atoms.claim: The description states that situation in the words a user's request would use.
atoms.quote: in the words a request would use

atoms.claim: The description gives that situation in one or two phrases, not a list of synonyms.
atoms.quote: one or two phrases, not a list of synonyms

sentences.text: Name the situation, never the material the skill produces; inspire-excellence is the cautionary case, a trigger built from the vocabulary of its own prompts that fired on its own output.

mentions.note: 'its' is inspire-excellence, not the trigger: the prompts are what the skill writes.
'that' attaches to the trigger, not to the prompts: the trigger is what fired.

atoms.claim: A skill's description names the situation that calls for the skill, not the material the skill produces.
atoms.quote: Name the situation, never the material the skill produces

atoms.claim: The inspire-excellence skill's trigger was built from the vocabulary of the prompts the skill writes, and it fired on the skill's own output.
atoms.quote: a trigger built from the vocabulary of its own prompts that fired on its own output

atoms.claim: The inspire-excellence trigger fired on the skill's own output because it was built from that output's vocabulary.
atoms.quote: built from the vocabulary of its own prompts
atoms.note: The passage sets the two facts side by side and leaves the cause to the reader.

sentences.text: Add a boundary ("not for X; use Y") only where two skills collide.

links.gloss: Sentence 3's single purpose for the description is why a boundary is limited to skills that collide.

atoms.claim: A skill's description includes a boundary only where another skill could be chosen for the same request.
atoms.quote: only where two skills collide
atoms.note: 'Collide' read as: both descriptions would match one request.

atoms.claim: A boundary takes the form 'not for X; use Y'.
atoms.quote: ("not for X; use Y")

sentences.text: Everything a loaded session reads belongs in the body: mechanism, rationale, file paths, history, which skill owns what.

links.there: a session scans to decide what to load
links.gloss: Sentence 1's session reads descriptions before loading anything; this session has loaded the skill and reads its body.
Sentence 3 gives the description one purpose; this sentence sends everything else to the body.

atoms.claim: Whatever a session reads after loading a skill belongs in the skill's body.
atoms.quote: Everything a loaded session reads belongs in the body

atoms.claim: Mechanism, rationale, file paths, history, and which skill owns which topic are things a session reads after loading a skill.
atoms.quote: mechanism, rationale, file paths, history, which skill owns what

atoms.claim: A skill's description leaves out mechanism, rationale, file paths, history, and which skill owns what.
atoms.quote: belongs in the body
atoms.note: The passage says where these go and leaves the reader to infer where they do not.

sentences.text: Aim for 150 characters; past 250, the excess needs a reason.

links.gloss: The length targets exist because the listing's space is limited.

atoms.claim: Aim for a skill description of about 150 characters.
atoms.quote: Aim for 150 characters

atoms.claim: A skill description longer than 250 characters needs a reason for the extra length.
atoms.quote: past 250, the excess needs a reason

sentences.text: A skill that is only ever summoned takes `disable-model-invocation: true` and a one-line description of what it does.

mentions.quote: A skill that is only ever summoned
mentions.note: 'Summoned' here is the web-tools skill library's term for a skill invoked by name only. Sentence 4's 'the situation that summons it' appears to use the verb more loosely, for whatever brings a skill in.

links.here: a one-line description of what it does
links.there: then the situation that summons it
links.gloss: Sentence 4 asks for what the skill does and then the situation; this sentence changes that for skills that are only summoned.

links.there: a session scans to decide what to load
links.gloss: Sentence 1 describes how a session chooses skills; this sentence names skills outside that choice.

atoms.claim: A skill that is only ever invoked by name sets disable-model-invocation: true in its frontmatter.
atoms.quote: takes `disable-model-invocation: true`

atoms.claim: A summoned-only skill's description is one line saying what the skill does.
atoms.quote: a one-line description of what it does

atoms.claim: A summoned-only skill's description omits the situation that summons it.
atoms.quote: of what it does
atoms.note: Read against sentence 4, which asks for what the skill does and then the situation. This sentence keeps only the first.

atoms.claim: A summoned-only skill is not chosen through a session's decision about what to load.
atoms.quote: only ever summoned
atoms.note: Inferred from the flag's name and the context's 'summoned-only'. The passage does not say how the platform lists such a skill.
